title: Light decode handoff: confidence guards and kernel-fallback plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a lightweight, low-risk speculative decode handoff that reduces mean time-to-first-token for common short responses while keeping cost and correctness regressions tightly bounded. Existing heavy-weight speculative routers add scheduling overhead and complex kernel affinity bookkeeping. Goal: implement a small-footprint handoff that uses a short prefill probe, a calibrated confidence guard, and an explicit kernel-mapped fallback pathway tied to runtime cost/latency SLOs. The design should be compatible with Dedicated and Hosted deployments, require no cross-tenant state, and be controllable via runtime route config.

Scope: prototype runtime adaptor, telemetry metrics, canary rollout config, and runbook for fallbacks. Not in scope: full multi-model gating/ensemble scoring, persistent historical trust models, or major GPU kernel rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: P95 end-to-end first-token latency improved by >=12% for short-response class (<=64 tokens) on synthetic short workload vs baseline without speculative handoff
False-acceptance rate (cases where speculative output is accepted but later judged lower-quality than baseline) <= 0.6% on evaluation prompt set (prompt-set-v2)
Integrated kernel-fallback triggers correctly route to alternate kernel/model when probe confidence < threshold or when per-request latency budget is threatened
Feature gated behind route flag and opt-in canary; rollout toggle and automatic rollback via Console if error-rate or quality regressions exceed thresholds
Telemetry dashboards (latency, cost-per-token, false-acceptance, fallback-rate) live and populated in staging before production canary
implementation_notes: Introduce a 3-step fast-path: (1) lightweight prefill probe using 8-token prefix on candidate small model variant; (2) calibration function produces confidence score with kernel-affinity hint; (3) on confidence >= threshold, accept speculative tokens and continue decode on chosen model; else fall back to full prefill-decode path

Calibration: use logistic regressor trained on prefills (features: probe log-prob mean, top-k entropy, delta to baseline model probe, GPU kernel fingerprint, request token-length estimate). Initial weights from offline eval; runtime updates via periodic batch re-calibration

Kernel mapping: runtime maintains small table of kernel fingerprints -> preferred execution kernel and a compatible fallback kernel. Handoff should annotate request with kernel_hint and fallthrough_kernel to avoid expensive on-path lookup

Fallback triggers: timed (if prefill probe + decode exceeds request latency budget - 60%), confidence threshold, or mismatch on structured-output constraints (e.g., JSON schema violation). Fallback must cancel speculative downstream work and reconstruct prefix if needed

Cost accounting: track speculative_write_token_count and rollback_token_count; surface delta on cost dashboards. Speculative tokens must be billed only when accepted; internal accounting will adjust when rollbacks occur
Runtime API: add optional fields to inference request metadata: speculative_probe_config (probe_len, model_hint, kernel_hint) and speculative_accept_metric. Default off unless route flag enabled
Compatibility: ensure path works when KV cache is used: speculative probe must install minimal KV entries or use ephemeral KV with deterministic merge into primary KV on accept
Testing: unit tests for probe calibration function, integration test covering accept+continue and accept+rollback, stress tests under high concurrency to observe queuing impacts
risks_mitigation: Risk: speculative acceptance introduces subtle quality regressions — mitigate by conservative initial threshold and short canary with synthetic prompts and user-facing prompts from non-critical traffic
Risk: KV cache divergence on speculative accept/rollback — mitigate by ephemeral KV with a transactional merge step and validation on accept
Risk: added scheduling complexity increases tail latency under bursty load — mitigate by bounded probe budget and early-circuit if worker queue length > configured limit
Risk: incorrect kernel mapping could degrade throughput — mitigate with kernel affinity sanity checks and automatic fallback kernel that is broadly compatible (slower but safe)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (feature flag gated): unit/integration tests + load tests in staging. Verify dashboards and billing counters
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for 1% internal traffic on Hosted. Monitor false-acceptance, P95 latency, and rollback-rate for 72 hours
Phase 2 (customer canary): expand to 3 pilot customers that have opted-in; run 1 week with daily QA prompts and manual review of borderline acceptances
Phase 3 (incremental ramp): sequentially increase traffic 3% -> 10% -> 30% with automated rollback if any metric breach occurs
Rollback criteria: false-acceptance > 1% absolute; P95 latency regression > +15% or increased error-rate (5xx) > +0.5% over baseline
telemetry_and_metrics: End-to-end P50/P95 first-token latency for short-response cohort
